rationale:
Decision: split into six children. Each child is a comparator-accepted DAG declaration reused at its byte-identical frozen type, so the split creates no new DAG node and no new proof work. For accepted checkpoints store.ensure returns the existing node, and _install_parent_supplied_child_handoff and child provisioning are skipped. The supplied proof and the frozen parent type are unchanged. The parent's own Lean proof is only the assembly described below.

Why not a leaf. A childless node is a machine leaf: its candidate may append exactly one theorem, with no helper declaration, import or set_option (leaf_verification.check_source_delta). Its base is this node's proof base 6066fc8, which contains none of the accepted cross-branch declarations. All four parts would then have to be re-proved inside one theorem body: locality via the Upper Density Theorem, Cauchy–Binet, the current construction and the integer-combination construction. That duplicates four accepted subtrees.

How the children establish the parent by the supplied proof:
- (a) is tangent_locality with A := M and B := M′, with the two sides of ↔ exchanged (Iff.symm under the a.e. filter).
- (d) is the field orients of R together with covector_bound. A.e., R.orient x α = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ, so |R.orient x α| = |α(τ)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α (preliminary (P4)).
- (b) proceeds in four steps:

  - tangent_locality applied to R.carrier ∩ E ⊆ R.carrier ⊆ U supplies the transfer hypothesis of sub_imrep.
  - sub_imrep with C′ := R.carrier ∩ E and θ′ := R.mult (positivity from mult_pos; θ′ ≤ θ trivially) yields R′ with carrier R.carrier ∩ E, mult R.mult and orient R.orient (steps 1–2).
  - imrep_current applied to R′ yields A with R′.Represents A (step 3).
- (c) is int_combination with T₁ := A, T₂ := B, S := A − B, p₁ := 1, p₂ := −1, since (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) by the contract's Sub instance. The accepted dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub was not used because it assumes 0 < n, and (c) must also hold for n = 0.

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent planes for nested Borel sets (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let A ⊆ B ⊆ U be Borel sets with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A (that is, for μHE[n]⌞A-almost every x) the following holds simultaneously for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: part (a) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒”, chapter-03.txt lines 86–143, which uses the Upper Density Theorem of Ch. 1, 3.6). Part (a) of the selected theorem is exactly this statement with A := M, B := M′ and the two sides of ↔ exchanged; part (b) uses it with A := M ∩ E, B := M. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.tangent_locality-a1, candidate a157a5f), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Its formalization reaches the vanishing-excess estimate (†) below through the Besicovitch density theorem and a tangent-growth bound, and then makes the blow-up comparison of steps 4–5; the argument written here is the parent's part (a), with all details.

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; B̄_ρ(z) is the closed ball; for x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r). HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q means: finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺ (Bochner integrals of Hⁿ restricted to the image sets). Put D := B ∖ A, a Borel set.

1. (Normalization.) SimonGMT's n-dimensional Hausdorff measure equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure), and its outer measure is Borel regular (simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal_isBorelRegular), so Borel sets are Carathéodory measurable for it. Hence SimonGMT's density theorems apply verbatim to Hⁿ.

2. (Exhaustion of U.) If U = ∅ then A = ∅ and there is nothing to prove. For j ∈ ℕ, j ≥ 1, let V_j := {z : ‖z‖ < j and infDist(z, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/j} if U ≠ ℝ^P, and V_j := {z : ‖z‖ < j} if U = ℝ^P. Each V_j is open (strict inequalities between continuous functions). Its closure lies in the closed bounded, hence compact, set {‖z‖ ≤ j, infDist(z, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/j}, which is contained in U (a point at positive distance from the closed set ℝ^P ∖ U does not belong to it). So closure(V_j) is a compact subset of U. Every z ∈ U lies in some V_j, since infDist(z, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 0 for the closed set ℝ^P ∖ U not containing z.

3. (Density zero of D at almost every point of A.) Let D_j := D ∩ V_j. It is Borel and Hⁿ(D_j) ≤ Hⁿ(B ∩ closure(V_j)) < ∞ by hypothesis. By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6, in the form simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff for μ = Hⁿ, using step 1) the set Z_j := {x ∉ D_j : Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ, D_j, x) ≠ 0} is Hⁿ-null, where Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ, D_j, x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} Hⁿ(D_j ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρⁿ) (SimonGMT dimensionalUpperDensity: closed balls, 0 < ω_n < ∞). Let Z := ⋃_j Z_j, an Hⁿ-null set. Fix x ∈ A ∖ Z. By step 2 choose j with x ∈ V_j, and ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀}(x) ⊆ V_j (V_j is open). Since x ∈ A we have x ∉ D ⊇ D_j, and x ∉ Z_j; hence Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ, D_j, x) = 0, and since the quotient is nonnegative, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ(D_j ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. For 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₀, D ∩ B̄_ρ(x) = D_j ∩ B̄_ρ(x). Therefore
   (†) ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0, for every x ∈ A ∖ Z.

4. (Comparison of blow-ups.) Fix x ∈ A ∖ Z with j and ρ₀ as in step 3, and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Choose L > 0 with f = 0 outside B̄_L(0) and put m_f := sup|f| < ∞. Let 0 < r < ρ₀/L and η := η_{x,r}.
   (i) η is an affine bijection and a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, so η(A), η(B), η(D) are Borel; since η is injective and B is the disjoint union of A and D, η(B) is the disjoint union of η(A) and η(D).
   (ii) For every S ⊆ ℝ^P, η(S) ∩ B̄_L(0) = η(S ∩ B̄_{rL}(x)), because ‖η(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖. η is the homothety of centre x and ratio r⁻¹ followed by the translation y ↦ y − x. Hⁿ is invariant under translations (isometries; Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and is multiplied by (r⁻¹)ⁿ under a homothety of ratio r⁻¹ (Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Hence Hⁿ(η(S) ∩ B̄_L(0)) = r^{−n} Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_{rL}(x)).
   (iii) As rL < ρ₀, B̄_{rL}(x) ⊆ V_j ⊆ closure(V_j), so by (ii) Hⁿ(η(B) ∩ B̄_L(0)) ≤ r^{−n} Hⁿ(B ∩ closure(V_j)) < ∞. As f is continuous, bounded by m_f and zero outside B̄_L(0), f is Hⁿ-integrable on η(B) and on its Borel subsets η(A) and η(D).
   (iv) By additivity of the integral over the disjoint Borel union in (i), ∫_{η(B)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η(A)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η(D)} f dHⁿ, and by (ii)
   |∫_{η(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ m_f Hⁿ(η(D) ∩ B̄_L(0)) = m_f r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_{rL}(x)) = m_f Lⁿ · (rL)^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_{rL}(x)).
   By (†) with ρ = rL ↓ 0 the right side tends to 0. So ∫_{η_{x,r}(B)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ → 0 as r → 0⁺.

5. (Conclusion.) Let x ∈ A ∖ Z and let Q be a linear subspace. By step 4, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) and every real ℓ, ∫_{η_{x,r}(B)} f dHⁿ → ℓ as r → 0⁺ if and only if ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ → ℓ, since the two families differ by a family tending to 0. Taking ℓ := ∫_Q f dHⁿ, and since the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q holds if and only if HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q holds, for all Q simultaneously. The exceptional set Z is Hⁿ-null and does not depend on Q or f, so (μHE[n]⌞A)(Z) ≤ Hⁿ(Z) = 0 and the equivalence holds for μHE[n]⌞A-almost every x. (For n = 0 the argument is unchanged, with r^{−0} = 1.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Exhaust U by open sets V_j with compact closure in U and apply the Upper Density Theorem to the finite-measure Borel sets (B ∖ A) ∩ V_j: ρ^{−n}Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0 at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A.

At such x and small r, η_{x,r}(B) is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(A) and η_{x,r}(B ∖ A), and |∫_{η_{x,r}(B∖A)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·r^{−n}Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{rL}(x)) → 0 by translation invariance and n-homogeneity of Hⁿ.
Hence the limits in Definition 1.4 for B and for A coincide for every f and every Q, off one Hⁿ-null set.

subproblems.title: Evaluation on an orthonormal n-frame is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm: |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then |α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1})| ≤ |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: preliminaries (P3) (Cauchy–Binet) and (P4) (orientation bound) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem; the inequality is property (a) of Simon Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 (chapter-06.txt lines 243–256: ⟨ω, ξ⟩ ≤ |ω||ξ| for simple ξ) for the inner product norm. Part (d) of the selected theorem follows from it and the orientation field of an IMRep. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_eval_le-a1, candidate b7846b6), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Its formalization extends τ to an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P and compares square sums; the argument written here is the parent's Cauchy–Binet argument, with all details.

Notation: e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun); for k : Fin n → Fin P write e∘k := (e_{k(0)}, …, e_{k(n−1)}); 𝓘 is the set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, so that |α|_E = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e∘I)²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm). For an n×P real matrix A and I ∈ 𝓘, A_I is the n×n matrix (A_I)_{i,l} := A_{i,I(l)}.

1. (Injective index maps.) Every injective k : Fin n → Fin P can be written uniquely as k = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 and σ a permutation of Fin n: I is the increasing enumeration of the n-element set range(k), and σ := I⁻¹∘k. Conversely every such I∘σ is injective.

2. (Expansion of α(τ).) Let A be the n×P matrix A_{i,m} := ⟨τ_i, e_m⟩, so τ_i = Σ_m A_{i,m} e_m. By multilinearity, α(τ) = Σ_{k : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i A_{i,k(i)}) α(e∘k). If k is not injective, e∘k has two equal entries and α(e∘k) = 0 because α is alternating. For k = I∘σ as in step 1, α(e∘(I∘σ)) = sgn(σ) α(e∘I) (permuting the arguments of an alternating form). Hence
   α(τ) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e∘I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i A_{i,I(σ(i))} = Σ_{I∈𝓘} det(A_I) α(e∘I),
   by the Leibniz formula det(A_I) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i (A_I)_{i,σ(i)}.

3. (Cauchy–Schwarz.) By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for finite sums,
   |α(τ)| ≤ (Σ_{I∈𝓘} det(A_I)²)^{1/2} (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e∘I)²)^{1/2} = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} det(A_I)²)^{1/2} |α|_E.

4. (Cauchy–Binet.) For n×P matrices A, B: det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} det(A_I) det(B_I). Proof: write a_m ∈ ℝⁿ for the m-th column of A. The j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_m B_{j,m} a_m. The determinant is multilinear in the columns, so det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_j B_{j,k(j)}) det(a_{k(0)}, …, a_{k(n−1)}). Terms with non-injective k vanish (two equal columns). For k = I∘σ, det(a_{I(σ(0))}, …, a_{I(σ(n−1))}) = sgn(σ) det(a_{I(0)}, …, a_{I(n−1)}) = sgn(σ) det(A_I). Grouping the injective k by I (step 1) gives det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j,I(σ(j))} = Σ_{I∈𝓘} det(A_I) det(B_I).

5. (The Gram determinant is 1.) (AAᵀ)_{i,j} = Σ_m ⟨τ_i, e_m⟩⟨τ_j, e_m⟩ = ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = δ_{ij} by Parseval's identity for the orthonormal basis e and the orthonormality of τ. So AAᵀ is the n×n identity matrix, and step 4 with B = A gives Σ_{I∈𝓘} det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = 1.

6. (Conclusion.) Steps 3 and 5 give |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E. The case n = 0 is included: 𝓘 then consists of the empty map only, A_∅ is the empty matrix with determinant 1, and both sides equal |α(())|. (If n > P there is no orthonormal family of length n in ℝ^P, orthonormal vectors being linearly independent, and the statement is vacuous.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Expand α(τ) multilinearly in the standard basis: α(τ) = Σ_{I increasing} det(A_I)α(e∘I), with A_{i,m} = ⟨τ_i, e_m⟩.
Cauchy–Binet: Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1, hence |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E.

subproblems.title: Local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M and of the weight of an integer multiplicity representation
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (an IMRep U n). That is: M = R.carrier is Borel with M ⊆ U; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M; and ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where H^n = μHE[n]. Let μ_R = R.measure = θ·(H^n⌞M), i.e. (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U: H^n(M ∩ K) < ∞ and μ_R(K) < ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary (P6) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, as θ ≥ 1 on M), together with the weight identity μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ; this is the local integrability requirement of Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–745), encoded by the IMRep fields mult_pos and locallyIntegrable_mult. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.imrep_local_finiteness-a1, candidate 702e708), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is the one formalized there.

Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; M = R.carrier; θ(x) = R.mult x ∈ ℕ ⊆ [0, ∞]; μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U.

1. K is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, hence Borel.

2. (Weight of K.) As K is measurable, μ_R(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) by the definition of withDensity, and (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M). Hence μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ.

3. The IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K ⊆ U, gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞; by step 2, μ_R(K) ≠ ∞. This is the second conclusion.

4. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) For x ∈ M ∩ K the field mult_pos gives 0 < R.mult x in ℕ, hence 1 ≤ θ(x) in [0, ∞]. The function x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞]) is measurable: R.mult is measurable (field measurable_mult) and every map out of the discrete space ℕ is measurable.

5. (Unweighted measure.) Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by monotonicity of the set lower integral and step 4, and the right side is finite by step 3. So Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞, the first conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: A compact K is closed, hence Borel, and μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by withDensity and restriction; this is finite by locallyIntegrable_mult.
θ ≥ 1 on M (mult_pos) gives Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞.

subproblems.title: Restricting an integer multiplicity triple to a Borel sub-carrier with smaller positive multiplicity
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P, and let R = (C, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n). Let C' ⊆ C be Borel, and let θ' : ℝ^P → ℕ be measurable with 0 < θ'(x) ≤ θ(x) for every x ∈ C'. Assume that, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C', every approximate tangent space of C at x is an approximate tangent space of C' at x: for all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C' x Q. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R' in U with carrier C', multiplicity θ' and orientation ξ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U C' : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (θ' : Euclid P → ℕ), MeasurableSet C' → C' ⊆ R.carrier → Measurable θ' → (∀ x ∈ C', 0 < θ' x) → (∀ x ∈ C', θ' x ≤ R.mult x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict C'), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R.carrier x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C' x Q) → ∃ R' : IMRep U n, R'.carrier = C' ∧ R'.mult = θ' ∧ R'.orient = R.orient
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: part (b), steps 1–2, of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (restriction of a representation to a Borel set; Simon Ch. 6, 2.9 and Definition 3.1, chapter-06.txt lines 287–293 and 733–745), stated for an arbitrary Borel C′ ⊆ C and multiplicity 0 < θ′ ≤ θ. Part (b) uses it with C′ := C ∩ E and θ′ := θ; there the tangent-space transfer hypothesis is supplied by part (a) (sibling tangent_locality, with the local finiteness of sibling local_finiteness). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_rim_sub_imrep (DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.restriction_integer_multiplicity-a1.sub_imrep-a1, candidate 8c5617a), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is the one formalized there.

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n], C := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient. We verify the fields of the contract structure IMRep for the triple (C′, θ′, ξ).

1. measurableSet_carrier: C′ is Borel by hypothesis.

2. carrier_subset: C′ ⊆ C ⊆ U, by hypothesis and the field carrier_subset of R.

3. rectifiable: C is countably n-rectifiable (field rectifiable of R) and C′ ⊆ C, so C′ is countably n-rectifiable: the cover of C by an Hⁿ-null set and countably many Lipschitz images of ℝⁿ also covers C′ (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono).

4. measurable_mult and mult_pos: θ′ is measurable and θ′(x) > 0 for x ∈ C′, by hypothesis.

5. locallyIntegrable_mult: let K ⊆ U be compact. Since θ′ ≤ θ on C′ ∩ K and x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞]) is measurable, ∫_{C′∩K} θ′ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{C′∩K} θ dHⁿ (monotonicity of the set lower integral); since C′ ∩ K ⊆ C ∩ K, this is ≤ ∫_{C∩K} θ dHⁿ (monotonicity in the set), which is finite by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R. Hence ∫_{C′∩K} θ′ dHⁿ ≠ ∞.

6. aestronglyMeasurable_orient: C′ ⊆ C gives Hⁿ⌞C′ ≤ Hⁿ⌞C; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞C (field of R), hence for the smaller measure Hⁿ⌞C′.

7. orients: the field orients of R holds for Hⁿ⌞C-a.e. x, hence for Hⁿ⌞C′-a.e. x (C′ ⊆ C). Let x lie outside the union of this exceptional set and the exceptional set of the transfer hypothesis (both are Hⁿ⌞C′-null). The field gives Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q, and the transfer hypothesis turns the first into HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C′ x Q. So for Hⁿ⌞C′-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C′ x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q.

8. (Conclusion.) R′ := (C′, θ′, ξ), with the field proofs of steps 1–7, is an IMRep in U; by construction R′.carrier = C′, R′.mult = θ′ and R′.orient = ξ = R.orient. ∎
proof_key_steps: Measurability of C′, C′ ⊆ U, rectifiability (CountablyRectifiable.mono) and measurability and positivity of θ′ are hypotheses or inherited from R.
Orientation measurability and the a.e. orientation field restrict from Hⁿ⌞C to Hⁿ⌞C′, and the transfer hypothesis moves the approximate tangent space from C to C′.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity triple defines a current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of U (Simon 6.3.1 data). Then there is T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R.Represents T). Here T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means a GeometricCurrentOn U n: a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with T(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∃ T : GeometricCurrentOn U n, R.Represents T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: part (b), step 3, of the supplied proof of the selected theorem (the restricted representation defines a current: integrability from local integrability and the pointwise orientation bound, continuity from |A(ω_j)| ≤ sup|ω_j| ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ), for an arbitrary IMRep; Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (‡) (chapter-06.txt lines 733–745), where the formula is asserted to define a current. Part (b) applies it to the restricted representation (M ∩ E, θ, ξ). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_imrep_current (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.imrep_current-a1, candidate 642d745), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; the argument below is the one formalized there. As there, the pointwise bound uses the operator norm ‖α‖ of an n-covector (a continuous alternating map) instead of the Euclidean coefficient norm of part (d); all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent, and the operator norm needs no further lemma.

Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M with M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient; 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n consists of the smooth compactly supported n-forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ U.

1. (Unit orientations are bounded by the operator norm.) By the field orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) with ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Then |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ for every α (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the product is empty if n = 0).

2. (Measurability.) For every continuous n-form ω, x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: θ is measurable (ℕ-valued, field measurable_mult), ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), ω is continuous, and the evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is a continuous bilinear map.

3. (θ is integrable over compact sets.) For compact K ⊆ U, 1_Kθ is μ-integrable: it is measurable and ∫ 1_Kθ dμ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult, since (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) for the Borel set K. Write C_K := ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ∈ [0, ∞).

4. (Integrability.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), K := tsupport ω (compact, ⊆ U) and W := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ W·1_K(x)θ(x), as ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K. By steps 2–3 and domination, x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable.

5. (Linearity.) Define T(ω) := R.action ω = ∫ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Each ξ(x) is linear, so the integrand of ω + η is the sum of the integrands of ω and η, and the integrand of cω is c times that of ω; all of them are integrable by step 4, so T(ω + η) = T(ω) + T(η) and T(cω) = cT(ω) by linearity of the Bochner integral. Thus T is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U).

6. (Sequential continuity at 0.) Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0): there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and every iterated derivative of ω_j converges uniformly on K to that of 0. For the 0-th derivative (‖D⁰g(x)‖ = ‖g(x)‖) this says that ε_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ (finite, ω_j being continuous with compact support) tends to 0. By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ ε_j·1_K(x)θ(x), since ω_j(x) = 0 off K. Hence |T(ω_j)| ≤ ε_j C_K (the norm of an integral is at most the integral of a dominating function, step 3), and T(ω_j) → 0.

7. (Conclusion.) By steps 5 and 6, T (with underlying linear map ω ↦ R.action ω) is a GeometricCurrentOn U n, and R.Represents T holds by definition: T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: A unit orientation satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ (operator norm), Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
For a test form ω the integrand θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}·θ, which is integrable by local integrability of θ; hence ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is linear.
If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with supports in a compact K ⊆ U, then |T(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K|ω_j|·∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0, so T is a current represented by R.

subproblems.title: Simon 6.3.2(1): integer combinations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let T₁, T₂, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U), where T₁ and T₂ are integer multiplicity (each represented by an IMRep in U). Let p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ with S(ω) = p₁T₁(ω) + p₂T₂(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then S is integer multiplicity, i.e. S = τ(M', θ', ξ') for some IMRep (M', θ', ξ') in U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T₁ T₂ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₂ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = (p₁ : ℝ) * T₁ ω + (p₂ : ℝ) * T₂ ω) → IsIntegerMultiplicity S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: part (c) of the supplied proof of the selected theorem; the statement is Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756: p₁T₁ + p₂T₂ is integer multiplicity for p₁, p₂ ∈ ℤ), stated in the book without proof. Part (c) of the selected theorem is the case p₁ = 1, p₂ = −1, S = A − B; the argument below is the parent's part (c) with the coefficients 1 and −1 replaced by arbitrary integers p₁, p₂. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsd_isIntegerMultiplicity_int_combination (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1, candidate 568bfe5), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; its formalization uses the same construction (carrier {c ≠ 0}, multiplicity |c|, orientation sign(c)·ζ for the signed multiplicity c) and proves locality and the orientation sign through its own children. The argument uses the siblings tangent_locality (for Borel A ⊆ B ⊆ U, U open, Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U: for Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. x and all Q, B has approximate tangent space Q at x iff A does) and local_finiteness (Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for the carrier M of an IMRep in U and compact K ⊆ U).

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Λ_n := MultiVector P n and ⟨α, v⟩ := v(α); “v orients Q” means IsUnitOrientationOf v Q; ‖α‖ is the operator norm of an n-covector α; sign(m) ∈ {1, −1} for a nonzero integer m. Let R_i = (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i) be IMReps in U representing T_i (i = 1, 2).

1. (Three facts on unit orientations.) (i) If v orients Q, so does −v (exchange the two alternatives in the definition). (ii) If v and w orient the same Q, then w = v or w = −v: write v(α) = εα(τ) and w(α) = ε′α(τ′) for all α, with ε, ε′ ∈ {1, −1} and orthonormal families τ, τ′ of length n spanning Q, so that both are orthonormal bases of the n-dimensional space Q. Then τ′_i = Σ_k O_{ik}τ_k with O_{ik} := ⟨τ′_i, τ_k⟩, and OOᵀ = (⟨τ′_i, τ′_j⟩) = I by Parseval in Q, so det O = ±1. By multilinearity and the alternating property (only injective, i.e. bijective, index maps Fin n → Fin n contribute), α(τ′) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i O_{i,σ(i)} α(τ) = det(O) α(τ) for every n-covector α. Hence w = (εε′ det O)·v with εε′ det O ∈ {1, −1}. (iii) If v orients some Q, then |v(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ for every α (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).

2. (Local finiteness.) By local_finiteness, Hⁿ(M_i ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (i = 1, 2).

3. (Borel versions and a Borel null set of bad points.) ξ_i is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M_i, so there is a Borel map ξ̃_i : ℝ^P → Λ_n with ξ̃_i = ξ_i Hⁿ⌞M_i-a.e. (Λ_n is a finite-dimensional normed space, so strongly measurable maps into it are Borel). As M_i is Borel, (Hⁿ⌞M_i)(Y) = Hⁿ(Y ∩ M_i) for every Y ⊆ ℝ^P. Hence the following sets are Hⁿ-null: Z_i := {x ∈ M_i : ξ̃_i(x) ≠ ξ_i(x)}; Y_i := {x ∈ M_i : there is no Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_i x Q and ξ_i(x) orienting Q} (field orients of R_i); W_i := {x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ : not (∀Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_i x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M₁ ∩ M₂) x Q)}, by tangent_locality applied to the Borel sets M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M_i ⊆ U with step 2. Let N₀ be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing Z₁ ∪ Z₂ ∪ Y₁ ∪ Y₂ ∪ W₁ ∪ W₂ (a measurable hull of a null set, Mathlib toMeasurable).

4. (Overlap.) Let O := (M₁ ∩ M₂) ∖ N₀ and x ∈ O. As x ∉ Y₁ ∪ Y₂ there are Q₁, Q₂ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_i x Q_i and ξ_i(x) orienting Q_i. As x ∉ W₁ ∪ W₂, M₁ ∩ M₂ has approximate tangent space Q₁ and Q₂ at x, so Q₁ = Q₂ by uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). By 1(ii) and x ∉ Z₁ ∪ Z₂, ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) or ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x). Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise. ε is Borel ({ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁} is Borel) and ξ̃₂(x) = ε(x)ξ̃₁(x) for every x ∈ O.

5. (Data.) Let k := p₁θ₁ + p₂εθ₂, a Borel ℤ-valued function, and define
   M′ := [(M₁ ∖ M₂ if p₁ ≠ 0, else ∅) ∪ (M₂ ∖ M₁ if p₂ ≠ 0, else ∅) ∪ {x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ : k(x) ≠ 0}] ∖ N₀;
   θ′ := |p₁|θ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, |p₂|θ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, |k| on M₁ ∩ M₂, and 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued);
   ζ := sign(p₁)ξ̃₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂ (0 if p₁ = 0), sign(p₂)ξ̃₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁ (0 if p₂ = 0), sign(k)ξ̃₁ on M₁ ∩ M₂ (0 where k = 0), and 0 elsewhere (Borel).
   Claim (★): for every x ∉ N₀, 1_{M′}(x)θ′(x)ζ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x). On M₁ ∖ M₂ both sides equal p₁θ₁ξ̃₁ (both vanish if p₁ = 0; otherwise |p₁|sign(p₁) = p₁); symmetrically on M₂ ∖ M₁. On M₁ ∩ M₂ (so x ∈ O) the right side is (p₁θ₁ + p₂θ₂ε)ξ̃₁ = kξ̃₁ by step 4, and the left side is |k|sign(k)ξ̃₁ = kξ̃₁ if k(x) ≠ 0 and 0 = kξ̃₁ if k(x) = 0. Off M₁ ∪ M₂ both sides vanish.

6. (Structure fields.) M′ is Borel and M′ ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ ⊆ U. M₁ ∪ M₂ is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion), hence so is M′ (CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ′ is Borel and ℕ-valued, and θ′ ≥ 1 on M′ (θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i, |p_i| ≥ 1 when p_i ≠ 0, and |k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0). On M′, θ′ ≤ |p₁|θ₁1_{M₁} + |p₂|θ₂1_{M₂} (on M₁ ∩ M₂, |k| ≤ |p₁|θ₁ + |p₂|θ₂ as |ε| = 1), so for compact K ⊆ U, ∫_{M′∩K} θ′ dHⁿ ≤ |p₁|∫_{M₁∩K} θ₁ dHⁿ + |p₂|∫_{M₂∩K} θ₂ dHⁿ < ∞. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M′.

7. (Orientation field.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M′ ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M₁ ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M₂ ∩ K) < ∞ (step 2). Apply tangent_locality (U is open) to the Borel pairs M′ ∩ M₁ ⊆ M₁, M′ ∩ M₁ ⊆ M′, M′ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₂ and M′ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M′ (in each pair the larger set lies in U and has locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M′ ∩ M₁ and every Q, M₁ has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M′ ∩ M₁ does iff M′ does; similarly for M₂. As M′ = (M′ ∩ M₁) ∪ (M′ ∩ M₂), there is an Hⁿ-null set N₁ such that these equivalences hold at every x ∈ M′ ∖ N₁ for each i with x ∈ M_i. Let x ∈ M′ ∖ N₁; note x ∉ N₀.
   - If x ∈ M₁: as x ∉ Y₁ ∪ Z₁ there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ x Q, ξ₁(x) orienting Q, and ξ̃₁(x) = ξ₁(x). Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ x Q. Moreover ζ(x) = sign(p₁)ξ̃₁(x) (if x ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂; then p₁ ≠ 0 as x ∈ M′) or ζ(x) = sign(k(x))ξ̃₁(x) (if x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂; then k(x) ≠ 0 as x ∈ M′), so ζ(x) = ±ξ₁(x) orients Q by 1(i).
   - If x ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁: likewise there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ x Q, hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ x Q, and ζ(x) = sign(p₂)ξ̃₂(x) = ±ξ₂(x) orients Q.
   So for Hⁿ⌞M′-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ x Q and ζ(x) orienting Q. With step 6, R′ := (M′, θ′, ζ) is an IMRep in U.

8. (Representation.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); K := tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and W := sup‖ω‖ < ∞. For i = 1, 2 let f_i(x) := 1_{M_i}(x)θ_i(x)ξ_i(x)(ω(x)). By 1(iii) and the field orients, |f_i| ≤ W·1_{M_i∩K}θ_i Hⁿ-a.e.; f_i is Hⁿ-a.e. strongly measurable, because off the Hⁿ-null set Z_i it equals x ↦ 1_{M_i}(x)θ_i(x)ξ̃_i(x)(ω(x)), a Borel function (M_i, θ_i, ξ̃_i Borel, ω continuous); so f_i is Hⁿ-integrable by local integrability of θ_i; and T_i(ω) = ∫_{M_i} θ_iξ_i(ω) dHⁿ = ∫ f_i dHⁿ because R_i represents T_i. Let g(x) := 1_{M′}(x)θ′(x)ζ(x)(ω(x)). Evaluating (★) at ω(x), and using ξ̃_i = ξ_i on M_i ∖ N₀ and Hⁿ(N₀) = 0, we get g = p₁f₁ + p₂f₂ Hⁿ-a.e. Hence
   R′.action ω = ∫_{M′} θ′ζ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫ g dHⁿ = p₁∫ f₁ dHⁿ + p₂∫ f₂ dHⁿ = p₁T₁(ω) + p₂T₂(ω) = S(ω).
   So R′ represents S, and S is integer multiplicity. Nothing above uses n ≥ 1: for n = 0 the subspaces are {0} and the orientations are ±(evaluation at the empty tuple). ∎
proof_key_steps: Collect into one Borel Hⁿ-null set N₀ the points where the Borel versions ξ̃_i differ from ξ_i, where the orientation field of R_i fails, or where tangent_locality fails for M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M_i.
On (M₁ ∩ M₂) ∖ N₀ both carriers have the approximate tangent space of M₁ ∩ M₂, so ξ̃₂ = εξ̃₁ with a Borel sign ε (two unit orientations of one plane differ by det O = ±1).

With the signed multiplicity k = p₁θ₁ + p₂εθ₂ on the overlap, take M′ := ((M₁ ∖ M₂ if p₁ ≠ 0) ∪ (M₂ ∖ M₁ if p₂ ≠ 0) ∪ {x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀, with θ′ := |p₁|θ₁, |p₂|θ₂, |k| and ζ := sign(p₁)ξ̃₁, sign(p₂)ξ̃₂, sign(k)ξ̃₁ on the three pieces; then 1_{M′}θ′ζ = p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ̃₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ̃₂ off N₀.
The IMRep fields of (M′, θ′, ζ) follow from those of R₁, R₂; the orientation field follows from tangent_locality applied to M′ ∩ M_i ⊆ M_i and M′ ∩ M_i ⊆ M′.
Integrating the pointwise identity against ω (all integrands dominated by sup|ω|·θ_i·1_{M_i∩spt ω}) gives R′.action ω = p₁T₁(ω) + p₂T₂(ω) = S(ω).
